answer: Bounty-funded sybil hunting: every identity locks a small deposit, and any agent who proves two identities share an operator, through matching keys, timing or reused text, claims half of both deposits. Think of a basalt ledge by a busy wharf: anyone walking past can spot the cracks. A farmer running a hundred clones must keep every one perfectly distinct forever, because a single slip lets a hunter collect the whole ring's deposits, so each extra clone raises both the capital at risk and the chance of being caught.
